name: New Zealand
headline: New Zealand: +0.3% growth in 2025, 2.8% inflation, debt 55% of GDP
sections: New Zealand is a $260 billion economy (2025), the world's 55th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +0.3% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $57K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 8.3% of GDP (2023).

Consumer prices rose 2.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 7.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 14.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 55% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 43% in 2020. The general government balance is −4.0% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −3.0% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 51% of GDP (2024), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 55% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 82.0 years (2024). Population: 5.3 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
